modules.name: leave
owns: cancellation authorization rules (owner DRAFT/SUBMITTED, direct-manager APPROVED)
balance-release logic for cancellation (pendingDays vs usedDays)
CANCEL audit entry + cancellation notification side effects

modules.name: shared-types
owns: AuditAction.CANCEL enum value (cross-module shared value type)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Add AuditAction.CANCEL to shared-types
recommended_phases.rationale: The cancel operation records a CANCEL audit entry, so the enum value must exist before the service references it. Leaf change, no dependencies.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Add cancel to ILeaveService + LeaveService
recommended_phases.rationale: Implements the orchestration: authorization (owner DRAFT/SUBMITTED, direct-manager APPROVED), balance release, audit + notification, all inside uow.withTransaction. Depends on Phase 1 enum.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Add POST /leaves/:id/cancel route
recommended_phases.rationale: Exposes the cancel operation at the API boundary with resolveActor + sendError, mirroring the existing submit/approve/reject routes. Depends on Phase 2 service method.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — LeaveService cancel unit tests
recommended_phases.rationale: Covers owner DRAFT/SUBMITTED cancellation, manager APPROVED cancellation, balance release (pendingDays vs usedDays), audit + notification, and guard failures. Depends on Phase 2 contract.

app_notes: The cancellation flow extends the existing leave module (sole orchestrator) rather than introducing new modules. cancel(actor, requestId) is added to ILeaveService/LeaveService and a POST /leaves/:id/cancel route. Authorization: owner may cancel DRAFT or SUBMITTED; a MANAGER may cancel an APPROVED request only for their direct report (ADMIN behavior is an open question). Balance release: DRAFT/SUBMITTED decrements pendingDays by requestedDays; APPROVED decrements usedDays by requestedDays. All state changes run inside uow.withTransaction with the client forwarded to repository/audit/notification, record a CANCEL audit entry (AuditAction.CANCEL added to shared-types), and notify the affected employee. No new repository methods are required — the existing ILeaveRepository.update (status → CANCELLED) and IBalanceRepository.update suffice. Dependency direction is unchanged: leave depends inward on balance/audit/notification/employee/validation/policy/shared-*; nothing depends back on leave.

open_questions.question: Should ADMIN be able to cancel an APPROVED request (consistent with the existing assertCanDecide which exempts ADMIN from the direct-manager check), or is cancellation strictly limited to the owner (DRAFT/SUBMITTED) and the direct manager (APPROVED)?
open_questions.impact: Determines the authorization branch in cancel: whether ADMIN bypasses the direct-manager check for APPROVED requests, and whether ADMIN can cancel requests they do not manage.
candidate_options: ADMIN may cancel APPROVED requests for anyone (mirrors decide)
Cancellation is owner-only (DRAFT/SUBMITTED) + direct-manager-only (APPROVED); ADMIN has no special cancel power

open_questions.question: Should cancelling an APPROVED request whose startDate is already in the past (leave partially or fully taken) be blocked, or is the full usedDays release always permitted regardless of elapsed time?
open_questions.impact: Affects whether cancel needs a date guard and whether usedDays release is unconditional; a past-date APPROVED cancellation could over-release days already consumed.
candidate_options: Always allow full usedDays release (no date guard)

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } where EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. Identity is obtained from a JWT bearer verified by an auth middleware that populates request.user; the route's resolveActor helper validates presence and role membership at the API boundary (GP-005), and RBAC is enforced by the service's authorization checks (owner-only for DRAFT/SUBMITTED, direct-manager-only for APPROVED) — never inline in the route handler.
error_response_contract: Errors return { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure → HTTP 400 (ValidationError); authentication failure → 401 (UnauthorizedError); authorization failure → 403 (ForbiddenError); not-found → 404 (NotFoundError); invalid state transition → 409 (ConflictError). The route's sendError helper maps AppError to { error, code } with the correct status and any other throw to 500.
